lens: mobile task completion, visual hierarchy, accessibility, and recovery

findings.observation: The new owned-action outcome path verifies a happy-path receipt but does not persist or reconcile its client operation after response loss. Each tap creates a new UUID, the UI keeps only an in-memory error and outcome field, and the service exposes no operation-status readback. If the backend commits and the response is lost, retry uses a different idempotency key and reaches a stale-revision rejection instead of recovering the committed receipt. The backend prevents a duplicate canonical mutation, but the phone cannot explain the already-recorded result or restore its receipt in place.
findings.evidence: Frozen source `apps/ios/Sources/Features/PursuitWorkspaceStore.swift:90-108` defaults `operationID` to a fresh UUID and retains no pending operation; `apps/ios/Sources/Features/RelationshipArchiveView.swift:1118-1135` records only an in-memory error on failure; `apps/ios/Sources/Services/PursuitWorkspaceClient.swift:36-64` exposes load and POST completion but no action-operation reconciliation. `docs/evaluations/2026-08-24-v1-final-panel-retest-02/evidence/pursuit-domain/pursuit-domain-runtime.json` proves server replay with the same key, while P0-02 response-loss coverage is for Proposal review and P0-07 covers only action happy-path/idempotent backend replay. The frozen iOS xcresults contain no action-outcome response-loss or relaunch test.
findings.user_impact: After a plausible mobile network drop, a recruiter can see `not verified`, retry, and then receive a conflict even though the outcome is already canonical. They must infer that closing and reloading may reveal completion, and they lose the durable receipt that should make a consequential state change trustworthy.
findings.recommendation: Persist the action operation ID, Pursuit/action revisions, outcome, and pending state before POST. On timeout, interruption, or relaunch, lock resubmission, reconcile the same idempotency key or canonical action readback, and restore either the exact applied receipt, a current conflict, or a truthful safe-to-retry state.
findings.verification: On iPhone 17 Pro and iPhone SE 375x667, use a proxy that commits action completion then drops the response. Background and terminate the app before readback, relaunch, and retry. Ten of ten runs must create exactly one action revision and receipt, reuse one operation key, never show premature success, and recover the canonical receipt without a second mutation or unexplained conflict.

findings.observation: Today now preserves every attention-bearing Pursuit and exposes outcome, target, blocker, evidence, owner, due work, and state, but it renders every field for every Pursuit in one uncollapsed feed. The frozen default Today has ten items while the first brief alone consumes most of a long iPhone 17 Pro viewport; at SE AX5, even one brief extends behind the persistent guide rail. When one Pursuit has both a Proposal and an owned action, the action title is the dominant headline but the primary button opens Proposal review, so the visual object and the tap result do not align cleanly.
findings.evidence: Frozen screenshots `evidence/screenshots/canonical-today.png` and `evidence/screenshots/se-375x667-ax5-today.png` under TS-V1-FINAL-20260824-02 show the ten-item count, full six-row brief, and small-screen density. `apps/ios/Sources/Features/RelationshipArchiveView.swift:375-421` renders every item without a cap and `:444-515` expands all decision context plus primary and secondary actions. `apps/ios/Sources/Domain/PursuitWorkspace.swift:56-91` selects the owned-action title when present but sets `Review proposal` as the primary action whenever a Proposal exists. Unit proof covers four uncapped items; the screenshot establishes ten, but no task study measures finding the first, middle, and final item.
findings.user_impact: The queue is complete but not glanceable. A recruiter managing many live searches must traverse a very long page, may open Proposal review when intending to update the due action, and cannot compare urgency across Pursuits without remembering content across screens.
findings.recommendation: Keep the no-cap invariant but use progressive disclosure: one compact summary row per Pursuit with outcome, due/owner, blocker/evidence state, and two explicitly named next steps when both review and action exist. Expand one brief in place or open the Pursuit for full context; do not hide or paginate away attention-bearing Pursuits.
findings.verification: With 10 and 50 mixed-state Pursuits at default and AX5, every item remains searchable and accessible. At least 9 of 10 first-use recruiters must find the highest-priority, fifth, and final Pursuit and open the intended Proposal versus owned action without a wrong destination; median first-target time stays under 10 seconds and no text is obscured by the persistent rail.

findings.observation: Canonical result surfaces still prioritize implementation identifiers and raw timestamps over human-readable confirmation. The same-name `Evidence synced` receipt lists only eight-character Person, role, context, Capture, and Resource prefixes; Proposal and action receipts expose truncated operation/actor IDs; Today and the completed action show raw fractional ISO timestamps because the freshness formatter falls back when parsing fails. These strings are traceable for engineers but not a calm recruiter receipt.
findings.evidence: Frozen screenshots `evidence/screenshots/same-name-binding-receipt.png`, `canonical-proposal-receipt.png`, `canonical-action-outcome.png`, and `canonical-today.png` under TS-V1-FINAL-20260824-02 show opaque IDs and strings such as `Observed 2026-08-24T02:57:08.067Z`. `apps/ios/Sources/Features/TextSignalCaptureView.swift:426-437` builds sync receipts from ID prefixes without Person/Pursuit labels; `apps/ios/Sources/Features/RelationshipArchiveSheets.swift:900-932` renders raw operation, actor, and occurredAt; `apps/ios/Sources/Domain/PursuitWorkspace.swift:468-485` falls back to the raw timestamp when `ISO8601DateFormatter` does not parse the fractional value present in the frozen fixture.
findings.user_impact: A recruiter cannot independently confirm which same-name Person and Pursuit received the evidence from the receipt itself, and must decode technical IDs and timestamps precisely where the interface should reduce post-action doubt.
findings.recommendation: Lead receipts with Person display name, identity clue, Pursuit title, role, action or changed field, localized observed time, and workspace-safe result. Keep stable ID prefixes in a secondary disclosure for audit support, and parse fractional ISO-8601 dates before rendering localized absolute plus relative time.
findings.verification: In the two-Alex-Chen fixture, ten first-use users must identify the selected Person/Pursuit and recorded result from the receipt alone with 100% accuracy. Snapshot tests for fractional timestamps, timezone changes, AX5, and Simplified Chinese must show localized dates with no raw `T...Z` string or identifier as the primary label.

findings.observation: The automated accessibility evidence is materially stronger in retest-02: the canonical Proposal, receipt, owned-action edit, and action receipt complete on iPhone SE 375x667 in dark mode at AX5 with Reduce Motion. However, no human has traversed the complete critical journey with VoiceOver, so focus order, edit-field announcements, selection state, error recovery, receipt semantics, and the dense multi-Pursuit Today queue remain unproven for a screen-reader user.
findings.evidence: Direct xcresult `/tmp/talent-signal-se-375x667-retest-02-r20.xcresult` contains three passed tests and `CandidateSignalUITests.swift:197-340` executes the canonical Proposal and owned-action journey at AX5. `docs/evaluations/2026-08-24-v1-final-panel-retest-02/evidence/ios-375x667-runtime.json` explicitly limits its claim to automated Simulator hierarchy/audits. Artifact TS-V1-FINAL-20260824-02 and `requirement-trace.json` both keep V1-TST-004 partial because manual VoiceOver is missing.
findings.user_impact: An automated pass can coexist with a blocking focus loop, ambiguous same-name option speech, unannounced state change, or unreachable recovery control. The release cannot yet claim that assistive-technology users can complete the same governed task.
findings.recommendation: Run a named human VoiceOver protocol on the frozen canonical journey at default size and SE AX5, including Today with ten Pursuits, same-name scope selection, exact evidence, each item decision, action outcome keyboard entry, response-loss recovery, both receipts, and deletion. Fix every critical-path speech, order, focus, or reachability defect before accessibility approval.
findings.verification: Retain a manual VoiceOver report with device/build, exact steps, spoken labels/values, focus order, state announcements, failures, and retest. The journey must complete without sighted assistance, crucial identity/evidence/effect text must be spoken before approval, and every failure or result must expose a reachable next step.

strengths: All 181 frozen source entries, 13 evidence files, nine screenshots, and the combined source manifest match the hashes in TS-V1-FINAL-20260824-02; the reviewed source and visible evidence are one coherent freeze.

The direct release-mode iPhone 17 Pro xcresult reports 95 passes, one documented legacy opt-in skip, and zero failures; the iPhone SE 375x667 dark AX5 xcresult reports three passes and now exercises canonical Proposal review plus owned-action outcome rather than a legacy review fixture.
Today no longer hides attention after an arbitrary display limit and now exposes outcome, target, blocker, evidence state, owner, due work, revision, and a no-action summary without ranking people.
Exact evidence, uncertainty, before/proposed/reason/effect, per-item decisions, revision checks, canonical readback, and empty external effects remain tightly coupled in Proposal review.

Same-name Text Signal capture provides two distinct human-readable scope options, requires explicit selection, preserves that binding across relaunch, and verifies stable Person, role, and context IDs after sync.
Audio capture is foreground-only, purpose- and authorization-gated, visibly local, supports revocation/deletion, and does not imply upload, transcription, Proposal creation, or external execution.
Server and Proposal recovery evidence covers duplicate submission, stale revision, deletion, offline retry, interruption, response loss, relaunch, and truthful success only after readback.
missing_evidence: Human manual VoiceOver traversal of the complete frozen mobile journey, including ten-item Today, same-name scope selection, Proposal item decisions, action outcome entry, recovery, receipts, and deletion.
Physical-device Action Button, microphone permission, route change, interruption, foreground capture, privacy indicator, and one-handed ergonomics evidence.
Credentialed live Claude Agent SDK trials remain `not_run_missing_credentials`; deterministic trials do not substitute for that release proof.
Production authentication, retention/deletion operations, regional controls, provider reconciliation, and cross-tenant adversarial evidence.
Authorized recruiter field comparison and candidate-side experience research; synthetic content is sufficient for the missing mobile usability study and real candidate data must remain excluded.
Action-outcome commit-then-response-loss, interruption, termination, relaunch, and receipt-reconciliation evidence on iOS.
The oldest supported iOS runtime, landscape, Increased Contrast, Reduce Transparency, Full Keyboard Access or Switch Control, and Low Power Mode on the canonical journey.
Simplified Chinese, 200% localization expansion, mixed-script long names, and right-to-left layout evidence for Today, scope selection, review, action outcome, and receipts.
Measured launch, scroll, tap-response, submit, retry, and refresh budgets on real hardware; XCTest duration is not product latency evidence.
First-use recruiter comprehension and search-time evidence for Today with 10 or more attention-bearing Pursuits.
open_questions: Which canonical operation-read endpoint should the iOS client use to reconcile an owned-action completion after response loss?
What maximum scan time and scroll distance define an acceptable uncapped Today queue at 10 and 50 Pursuits?
Which human-readable identity clue is safe and stable enough to lead a same-name sync receipt while full IDs remain secondary audit metadata?
What minimum iOS version and locale set define the V1 mobile release gate?
